conventions.convention: G is a finite simple graph; Q is an integer at least two; every edge activity is finite and nonnegative. Component counts include isolated vertices, and empty products equal one. The weights are mathematical objects without empirical or physical-unit claims.

Boundary wiring is an equivalence relation on B⊆V. kξ(A) counts all classes generated by wiring and occupied edges, including the wired boundary class. Discrete wiring is free boundary; this definition asserts no wired Potts spin marginal.
Independent uniform cluster coloring is asserted conditional only on edge sets of positive probability, under the unpinned finite Edwards–Sokal law.

The transfer initially activates every boundary vertex, accounts separately for isolated vertices outside B, and contributes Q exactly when a block loses its last active vertex. Connectivity joins are idempotent partition operations.

The loop identity uses a connected simple plane graph with all vertices free and no exterior wiring. The exterior face is one dual vertex; dual loops and parallel edges are retained. ℓ(A) counts boundary components of the disk-and-band neighborhood, including the single disk for an edgeless one-vertex graph. The loop value is the positive square root √Q.
Temperley–Lieb multiplication stacks the left factor above the right and assigns δ to each removed closed cycle. Its cup-cap generator is distinct from the idempotent FK connectivity join.

load_bearing.statement: For a finite simple graph, integer Q≥2 and finite activities v_e≥0, w_P(σ)=∏_e(1+v_e 1_{σ(u_e)=σ(w_e)}) and w_FK(A)=Q^{k_G(A)}∏_{e∈A}v_e. Their partition functions are the respective finite sums and are positive.

For every finite simple graph, integer Q≥2 and finite nonnegative activities, the stated joint weight W has Potts and FK marginals with Z_P=Z_FK. Conditional on any positive-probability edge set, its component colors are independent and uniform on [Q]. For every x,y∈V, P(σ(x)=σ(y))=1/Q+(1−1/Q)P_FK(x↔y).

For a finite simple graph, integer Q≥2, finite nonnegative activities, B⊆V and an equivalence relation ξ on B, kξ(A) is the number of classes of the least equivalence relation generated by ξ and occupied-edge endpoint pairs, and Zξ_FK=Σ_{A⊆E}Q^{kξ(A)}v_A.

For every finite simple graph, integer Q≥2, finite activities v_e≥0, edge order, boundary set B⊆V and equivalence relation ξ on B, the finite FK connectivity-transfer procedure terminates after finitely many operations and returns exactly Zξ_FK=Σ_{A⊆E}Q^{kξ(A)}∏_{e∈A}v_e. For discrete ξ it returns Z_FK.

For a finite connected simple plane graph with free vertices and exterior face, integer Q≥2 and finite activities v_e≥0, Z_FK(Q,v)=Q^{|V|/2}Σ_{A⊆E}(√Q)^{ℓ(A)}∏_{e∈A}(v_e/√Q), where ℓ(A) counts boundary loops of its occupied-edge disk-and-band neighborhood. The loop value is δ=√Q.

published_dependencies.used_for: Finite cardinalities, including the empty set and isolated-vertex counts.
The graph convention: finite vertex set and edges that are two-element vertex subsets.
Polygonal plane embeddings, complement faces, and facial side occurrences, including bridges traversed twice.
One dual vertex per face and one dual edge per primal edge, retaining loops and parallel edges.
Existence of the reciprocal dual embedding. The loop proof does not invoke the double-dual conclusion requiring a simple dual.
Euler counts for the spanning occupied subgraph and the disjoint polygonal boundary cycles.
Polygonal paths within complement faces in the dual-connectivity and neighborhood arguments.
Noncrossing matching diagrams, stacking orientation and closed-cycle weight. Its displayed cup-cap diagram agrees with its definition.
Well-defined associative stacking for local smoothing diagrams, without semisimplicity or faithfulness assumptions.

seams_checked.note: The upstream page is a declared reading prerequisite. Its four defining/statement interfaces were inspected; the assigned FK items invoke no large-deviation proposition or ensemble-limit conclusion.

The Swendsen–Wang algorithm and invariance proof retain the finite simple graph, integer Q≥2 and finite nonnegative activities. They use the exact unpinned Edwards–Sokal marginals and positive-probability cluster-color conditional; the edge conditional is derived locally.

The real-q boundary definition explicitly extends the earlier finite convention and verifies normalized-law agreement only in its stated integer/free special case. The Potts critical-temperature proof identifies the Edwards–Sokal supplier as unpinned and derives pinned coloring locally, including the configuration-independent Q^{-1} normalization factor.
